title: Graduated Introductory Allowance + Security-Questionnaire Credit Bonus (Windsor Experiment)
creator: Aisha Morrell
description: Experiment to replace the single flat trial credit model with a graduated introductory allowance (three cohort tiers) and a one-time security-questionnaire completion bonus. Goal: increase high-quality PLG conversions while limiting token-cost exposure and aligning upgrade prompts with meaningful usage signals. This combines behavioral nudges (usage anchors), expiry hygiene (soft expiry reminders + emergency buffer), and an enterprise-focused incentive (unlock extra credits for completing the security/RFI questionnaire). The experiment is designed to be measurable, reversible, and low-friction for new users.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 14-day activation rate (first 1000 tokens consumed) increases by >= 8% vs control
2) 30-day paid conversion rate (upgrade to paid plan or reserved capacity inquiry) increases by >= 3 percentage points for medium/high cohorts
3) Net token cost per paid conversion remains <= $45 (productionized token-cost calc)
4) No measurable increase in abuse/fraud signals (spam accounts, automated token drain) beyond baseline +2%
5) Security-questionnaire pathway yields >= 20% completion rate among invited enterprise trial accounts and 10% of those convert to sales-qualified leads within 60 days
comments: 2026-02-22 — Kickoff with Eng/Design/Product. Agreed cohort sizes: small(5k tokens), medium(25k), large(100k) introductory allowances. Priya to own cohort allocation logic and targeting rules.

2026-02-25 — Design reviewed: added 'soft expiry' UX (in-app banner at 7 days before expiry + one emergency buffer expiration extension). DES feedback: ensure banner copy emphasizes remaining dollar-equivalent and upgrade CTA that doesn't block API access.

2026-03-02 — Eng backlog: ENG-20134 to expose cohort attribute in signup API; ENG-20876 to add token-credit accounting and emergency buffer flow. Alpha implementation PR: github.com/redwood-inference/prod/PR-3841 (engineering requested load test plan).

2026-03-05 — Security asked to review the incentive for completing the RFI; suggested data minimization and opt-in consent language. Security will run questionnaire flow through privacy checklist before launch (security reviewer: Diego Ramos).
2026-03-09 — Analytics: dashboard template created in Looker: PLG > Windsor experiment (link below). Initial A/A checks scheduled for 3/12. Cohort holdback: 20% control across all traffic segments.
decision_rationale: Flat trial credits compress signal: small accounts exhaust quickly and churn, large credits are expensive and reduce urgency. Graduated allowances match early user usage patterns, improving signal-to-noise for PLG funnels. Tying a modest credit bonus to completing the enterprise security questionnaire creates a low-friction qualification mechanism for sales and reduces gating in the product while capturing intent from higher-value orgs.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (A/A validation) — 3/12 to 3/19: smoke tests and A/A to validate instrumentation
Phase 1 (Limited rollout) — 3/20 to 4/02: 10% of new signups split across cohorts + 20% control group
Phase 2 (Scaled rollout) — 4/03 to 4/14: 50% of new signups if Phase 1 metrics within safety thresholds
Full rollout or rollback decision — 4/15: Product to sign off based on acceptance criteria and fraud checks
metrics: Activation: percent of users consuming >1000 tokens in first 7 days
Conversion: percent converting to paid or contacting sales within 30 days
Token cost per conversion: total tokens consumed by cohort * token-unit-cost / conversions
RQI (Request Quality Index): percent of API requests with user-agent and prompt patterns consistent with human usage
Security RFI completion rate and SQO (sales-qualified-opportunity) creation rate
